answer: Randomized Inlet Assignment Scheme: each new agent identity is mapped at registration to one of many fixed admission inlets via a delay chosen from a beacon the attacker cannot predict, so identities cannot be precomputed or clustered in advance. Assignment opens only a short ivory window for activation, after which the identity expires unregistered. Identities co-located in the same virtual mesa must then independently pass randomized latency checks, forcing attackers to pay a distinct hardware and timing cost per surviving identity rather than one bulk cost.
